dimensions.label: Bonding ties
dimensions.definition: Strength, quality and density of close ties within families, friendship circles and neighborhoods.

dimensions.label: Bridging ties
dimensions.definition: Social ties that cross lines of class, race, religion or party.

dimensions.label: Civic participation
dimensions.definition: Membership, volunteering and taking part in organized and local public life.

dimensions.label: Generalized trust
dimensions.definition: Whether people expect unspecified others to be trustworthy, fair and helpful.

dimensions.label: Individual and family well-being
dimensions.definition: Emotional and material well-being of individuals and the households they live in.

dimensions.label: Belonging
dimensions.definition: A felt sense of being part of one's community and the country.

metrics.source: General Social Survey (NORC), cumulative file 1972-2024, release 3a
metrics.universe: US adults 18+ living in households (English or Spanish speakers since 2006)
metrics.se_method: Taylor linearization on VSTRAT/VPSU; Kish effective-n where design codes are absent (1972-1973)
metrics.state_gap: The public GSS file has no state identifiers (they are restricted-use), and the sample is not designed for state estimates.
metrics.series_note: Two series are shown and never joined. 'Interviewer' = in-person or phone interviews (TRUST etc.). 'Web' = web self-completion without a volunteered 'depends' option (TRUSTNV etc.), 2021-2024. In years with both, the web series runs several points higher, so the 2018-2021 change cannot be read as a real change.
metrics.label: Say most people can be trusted
metrics.plain: of adults say most people can be trusted
metrics.wording: Generally speaking, would you say that most people can be trusted or that you can't be too careful in dealing with people?
metrics.response_cut: Share answering 'most people can be trusted'. 'Depends' stays in the denominator.
metrics.measures: Generalized trust in unspecified others: an attitude reported to an interviewer or on a web form.
metrics.does_not_measure: Trust in neighbors, institutions or specific groups. Trusting behavior. Any state or local variation.

tags.text: The item is known to be sensitive to mode, question order and what 'most people' brings to mind for the respondent.

metrics.source: Household Trends and Outlook Pulse Survey (Census Bureau), published national tables
metrics.weight: Census person weights, as applied in the published tables
metrics.se_method: Census published SE tables; summed categories ignore covariance (approximate)
metrics.state_gap: HTOPS publishes national, regional and top-10 metro tables only, so there are no state estimates. Regional tables could be added.

metrics.label: Usually or always get the social and emotional support they need
metrics.plain: of adults usually or always get the social and emotional support they need
metrics.wording: Census table header: 'Obtains social and emotional support'. See the wave questionnaire for the full wording.
metrics.measures: Self-reported adequacy of emotional support: a measure of the quality of close ties.
metrics.does_not_measure: Who provides the support (family, friends, community) or whether the ties cross group lines.

metrics.does_not_measure: Quality of contact, or contact by phone or video (published separately and not shown).

metrics.source: Current Population Survey, September Civic Engagement and Volunteering Supplement (Census Bureau / AmeriCorps)
metrics.universe: Civilian non-institutional persons 16+ with a supplement interview (self or proxy response)
metrics.years_note: Asked with identical wording in 2019, 2021 and 2023. Earlier supplements used different items and are not included.
metrics.label: Talked with or spent time with neighbors at least a few times a month
metrics.plain: talk with neighbors at least a few times a month
metrics.wording: In the past 12 months, how often did you have a conversation or spend time with your neighbors?
metrics.response_cut: 'Basically every day', 'a few times a week' or 'a few times a month' (codes 1-3 of 6).
metrics.measures: Self- or proxy-reported frequency of contact with neighbors.
metrics.does_not_measure: Quality or warmth of the contact, felt belonging, or trust in neighbors.

tags.text: Neighbor ties are classed as bonding here (local, frequent ties), but neighbors may differ in class, race or politics, so these ties can also bridge.
Some answers are proxy reports by another household member, who may not know how often the person talks to neighbors.
The cut point (a few times a month or more) is this app's choice. AmeriCorps uses 'a few times a week or more' for 'frequently'.

metrics.source: Current Population Survey, September Civic Engagement and Volunteering Supplement (Census Bureau / AmeriCorps)
metrics.universe: Civilian non-institutional persons 16+ with a supplement interview (self or proxy response)
metrics.years_note: Asked with identical wording in 2019, 2021 and 2023. Earlier supplements used different items and are not included.
metrics.label: Exchanged favors with neighbors at least a few times a month
metrics.plain: exchange favors with neighbors at least a few times a month
metrics.wording: In the past 12 months, how often did you and your neighbors do favors for each other such as house sitting, watching each other's children, lending tools, and other things to help each other?
metrics.response_cut: Codes 1-3 of 6, the same cut as the conversation item.
metrics.measures: Reported reciprocal practical help between neighbors.
metrics.does_not_measure: Help within families or between friends who are not neighbors.

tags.text: Proxy reporting, and the bonding/bridging classification, as for the conversation item.

metrics.source: Opportunity Insights Social Capital Atlas (Chetty et al. 2022, Nature), county file
metrics.universe: Facebook users aged 25-44 in the US with sufficient friends and location data, 2018-2019
metrics.label: Friendship network clustering
metrics.plain: of a person's friend pairs are also friends with each other
metrics.se_method: No SE published for this measure
metrics.wording: Not a survey item. It is computed from Facebook friendship networks.
metrics.response_cut: Average share of a person's friend pairs who are also friends with each other.
metrics.measures: Density of friendship networks: how tightly knit people's circles are.
metrics.does_not_measure: Whether the ties are supportive, or whether they sit within or across social groups.

tags.text: The state values are this app's population-weighted aggregation of county estimates. Opportunity Insights does not publish state figures.
Dense networks can mean strong communities or closed ones. Higher is not simply better.

metrics.source: Opportunity Insights Social Capital Atlas (Chetty et al. 2022, Nature), county file
metrics.universe: Facebook users aged 25-44 in the US with sufficient friends and location data, 2018-2019
metrics.label: Friendship support ratio
metrics.plain: of friendships are embedded in at least one shared friend
metrics.se_method: No SE published for this measure
metrics.wording: Not a survey item. It is computed from Facebook friendship networks.
metrics.response_cut: Share of friendships within the county where the two friends have at least one other friend in common.
metrics.measures: How embedded friendships are in mutual networks, a structural proxy for support.

tags.text: The state values are this app's population-weighted aggregation of county estimates. Opportunity Insights does not publish state figures.

metrics.source: Opportunity Insights Social Capital Atlas (Chetty et al. 2022, Nature), county file
metrics.universe: Facebook users aged 25-44 in the US with sufficient friends and location data, 2018-2019
metrics.label: Economic connectedness (cross-class friendship)
metrics.plain: economic connectedness: 1.0 would mean friendships fully mixed across the income line
metrics.weight: Counties weighted by num_below_p50 (estimated number of below-median-SES people)
metrics.wording: Not a survey item. It is computed from Facebook friendship networks.
metrics.response_cut: 2 x the average share of above-median-SES friends among below-median-SES people. 1.0 = no class segregation in friendships, below 1 = fewer cross-class friends than an even mix would give.
metrics.measures: How often lower-income people's friendships reach across the income line.
metrics.does_not_measure: Ties across race, religion or party. Friendship quality. People not on Facebook. Any change over time (one snapshot only).

tags.text: The state values are this app's population-weighted aggregation of county estimates. Opportunity Insights does not publish state figures.
The sample covers Facebook users aged 25-44 only. OI reweights for representativeness, but platform selection bias remains.

metrics.label: Formally volunteered through an organization
metrics.plain: volunteered through an organization in the past year
metrics.wording: Census recode PRSUPVOL: 'yes' to 'spend any time volunteering for any organization or association' or to the follow-up prompt about infrequent or children's activities.
metrics.response_cut: PRSUPVOL = 1 (volunteer). Matches AmeriCorps' published formal volunteering rate.
metrics.measures: Formal volunteering through an organization in the past 12 months.
metrics.does_not_measure: Informal helping (see the favors item) or hours volunteered.

tags.text: PRSUPVOL has no missing category: people who did not answer are coded 'not a volunteer'.
2021 fieldwork fell during COVID-19, when many organizations had paused in-person volunteering.

metrics.source: General Social Survey (NORC), cumulative file 1972-2024, release 3a
metrics.universe: US adults 18+ living in households (English or Spanish speakers since 2006)
metrics.se_method: Taylor linearization on VSTRAT/VPSU; Kish effective-n where design codes are absent (1972-1973)
metrics.state_gap: The public GSS file has no state identifiers (they are restricted-use), and the sample is not designed for state estimates.
metrics.series_note: Two series are shown and never joined. 'Interviewer' = in-person or phone; 'Web' = web self-completion (2021-2024). Respondents were not randomly assigned to mode, so the gap mixes mode effects with differences in who answered by web.
metrics.label: Say they are very happy
metrics.wording: Taken all together, how would you say things are these days - would you say that you are very happy, pretty happy, or not too happy?
metrics.does_not_measure: Life satisfaction, purpose, or family well-being.

gaps.text: No public source gives repeated measures of felt belonging. Neighborhood contact is a behavior and is not used as a stand-in. Candidate for CAV's own survey.
No source in the app is weekly. The freshest (HTOPS) arrives about every two months, and most others every two years. The weekly page is a weekly check for new data, not a weekly measurement.

No state-level generalized trust. The 2019-2023 CPS supplements have no trust item, and the public GSS file has no state identifiers. [uncertain] Earlier CPS supplements may have had a neighbor-trust item. Not checked here.
Institutional trust (government, media, science) is a separate construct and is not included yet.
Only cross-class ties are measured. Cross-race, cross-religion and cross-party ties have no comparable public source here.
All bridging and network-density data are a single 2018-2019 snapshot, so there is no trend.
Family well-being is covered only by food sufficiency. Child well-being, family relationships and economic security beyond food are not included.
The JEC Social Capital Index (2018, state and county) is not included: the JEC site blocks automated downloads.
No composite cohesion score. The dimensions measure different constructs and are reported separately on purpose.
